options: The product of all the time constants
The sum over capacitors of \(C_iR_{Ci}\), each \(R_{Ci}\) found with all other capacitors open
The largest single \(C_iR_{Ci}\)
The sum with all other capacitors shorted

questions.prompt: How do you find the resistance \(R_{Ci}\) seen by one capacitor?
options: Short the other capacitors and measure to ground
Use the DC bias resistance at the node
Open the other capacitors, zero the independent sources and apply a test source across \(C_i\)'s terminals
Keep the input source active and measure the gain
questions.explanation: Voltage sources become shorts and current sources opens (reader Sec. 14.11.3).

options: \(C_L\), because it is the largest capacitor
\(C_{gs}\), because it is at the input
All three contribute equally
\(C_{gd}\), the smallest one: it is the largest \(RC\) product, not the largest \(C\), that matters
questions.explanation: \(C_{gd}\) sees a gain-multiplied resistance of 220 kΩ.

Unrelated to the true bandwidth

options: That the circuit is unstable
That the other capacitors set the bandwidth
That node sets the dominant pole, so the bandwidth is controlled there, as with a compensation capacitor
Nothing useful

questions.prompt: Preview of amplifier compensation: what does OCTC not tell you that a feedback designer needs?
options: The dominant pole
The DC gain
The sign of the gain
Where the second and higher poles are, which set the phase margin
questions.explanation: OCTC estimates \(\omega_1\) only; short-circuit time constants or full analysis find the rest.
